title: LHCb makes the first high-significance observation of the rare Σ⁺ → pμ⁺μ⁻ decay
summary: Using 5.4 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV proton-proton collision data collected in 2016–2018, LHCb observed 237 ± 16 Σ⁺ → pμ⁺μ⁻ decays and measured a branching fraction of (1.08 ± 0.17) × 10⁻⁸. The dimuon spectrum showed no evidence of resonant structures, and the results are compatible with Standard Model expectations. This is the first high-significance observation; earlier HyperCP and LHCb Run 1 results were evidence only.

evidence.tested: Using 5.4 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV proton-proton collision data collected in 2016–2018, LHCb observed 237 ± 16 Σ⁺ → pμ⁺μ⁻ decays and measured a branching fraction of (1.08 ± 0.17) × 10⁻⁸.
evidence.unknown: The paper reports an observation of the nonresonant rare decay, not evidence for the hypothetical intermediate X⁰ suggested by the earlier HyperCP candidates; no resonant dimuon structure is found. The measured branching fraction is compatible with Standard Model expectations. AI supported event selection and background reduction but is not the sole basis of the result.
evidence.ai_role: The BDT combined kinematic and geometric variables, trained on simulated signal and data sidebands representing combinatorial background, and was used in the final candidate selection. Its output threshold was optimized together with particle-identification and Λ-veto criteria to maximize expected significance. This classifier contributed to background suppression; it was one component of the analysis, alongside upgraded trigger selections, detector reconstruction, and the statistical fit.
